title: Graduation Day

beats.narrativeText: Director Orion welcomes the learner back to Explorer Academy Headquarters — the same briefing room where this all began, though it feels different walking in this time.
Something is clearly being celebrated today. But watching Director Orion, it's obvious this isn't about the mystery of Outpost Echo at all — it's about something else entirely.
The learner opens their Explorer Journal back to its very first page and reads forward — all the way from a nervous first entry to whoever they are now.
beats.trigger: Journal reviewed and journey reflected on

beats.narrativeText: It becomes clear what the Academy is actually celebrating: not what the learner found at Outpost Echo, but how they went about finding it — observing carefully, asking thoughtful questions, testing ideas, and being willing to change their mind when the evidence did.
The learner must pick out their favourite investigations from the whole campaign and put together a final expedition report — the last entry of the Outpost Echo mystery.
beats.trigger: Favourite investigations identified and report completed

beats.narrativeText: The probationary status that began with a single letter in Mission 1 officially ends. The learner is no longer being tested as a possible Explorer — they receive their Explorer Certificate as one.
Atlas shares something the learner didn't know until now: Outpost Echo was never the only expedition. Other stations, other teams, are out there right now investigating mysteries of their own.
Just as the celebration settles, a new transmission arrives — from a research station nobody has mentioned before. Whatever it is, it's clearly not finished being a mystery yet.

activities.title: Reflect on Your Learning Journey
activities.storyContext: Director Orion has welcomed the learner back to Explorer Academy Headquarters — the same room, the same Director, but a very different Explorer walking in this time.
activities.instructions: Reflect honestly on your entire journey through the campaign, from the first invitation to right now. What actually changed, not just what happened.
activities.output: A written reflection on the whole learning journey.

activities.title: Review Your Explorer Journal
activities.storyContext: The Explorer Journal has recorded every observation since Mission 1 — it's the one thing that's been with you for the entire expedition.
activities.instructions: Look back through your Explorer Journal from the very first entry, and notice anything that reads differently now than it did when you wrote it.
activities.output: Notes on what stands out from reviewing the journal.

activities.title: Identify Favourite Investigations
activities.storyContext: The Academy celebrates how the learner investigated, not just what they discovered — so this is about the investigations that mattered to you, not the ones that sound most impressive.
activities.instructions: Identify your favourite investigations from the campaign and explain specifically what made each one stand out.
activities.output: A list of favourite investigations with reasons.

activities.title: Complete Final Expedition Report
activities.storyContext: A final expedition report will close out the Outpost Echo investigation for good — the official record of how the mystery was actually solved.
activities.instructions: Complete a final expedition report summarising the whole campaign, as if it will be read by the next Explorer to visit Outpost Echo.

activities.title: Receive Explorer Status
activities.storyContext: The probationary status that began with a single letter in Mission 1 is officially over.
activities.instructions: Personalise your Explorer Certificate to mark officially becoming an Explorer — in your journal, or using the optional printable certificate, whichever feels right.

activities.title: Design Your Own Future Expedition
activities.storyContext: Atlas reveals that numerous other expeditions remain active across the world.
activities.instructions: Design your own future expedition — where would you go, and what would you investigate?
activities.output: A design for a future expedition.

activities.title: A Question With No Complete Answer
activities.storyContext: Real exploration never really ends — there are always new questions to investigate.
activities.instructions: Research a real-world scientific question that still has no complete answer.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What kind of Explorer have you become — and how is that different from who you were when you opened that first invitation in Mission 1?

discussionPoints: What kind of Explorer have you become?
What would you like to investigate next?
parentGuide.preparation: No special preparation required. Consider celebrating this milestone together.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for genuine reflection on growth across the whole campaign, not just a summary of what happened.

completionCriteria: Learning journey reflected on, favourite investigations identified, and final expedition report completed.
